To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Alcalase 240L is a good enzyme to hydrolyze PKEP into PKEPH.
PKEPH could be prepared by hydrolyzing the extracted PKEP using the proteases, Alcalase 24 L and Flavourzyme 500MG.

Alcalase 24L is the most effective enzyme to hydrolyze PKEP into PKEPH with high DH and short hydrolysis time, and the PKEPH could be utilized for various purposes such as in the production of functional food and nutraceuticals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of PKEP hydrolyzed with Alcalase 2400L and its potential utilization as a functional food ingredient.
the development of an enzymatic method for hydrolyzing PKEP and the production of PKEPH.
the production of PKEPH from the PKE, a palm oil byproduct, using an alkaline extraction method followed by enzymatic treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Alcalase 24L is the most efficient enzyme to produce PKEPH of the best DH% in shortest time.
Alcalase 24.4L was the most efficient enzyme to hydrolyze PKEP and produced PKEPH of 75.96% DH in 1 h of hydrolysis.
the most effective conditions for hydrolysis of PKEP using Alcalase® was at 8.0%, 50°C for one hour and for Pepsin was 8%, 50°C, for 6 hours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Alcalase® is the best enzyme for hydrolyzing PKEP into PKEPH, while Pepsin is the least.
Alcalase®2.4L was the best enzyme in hydrolyzing PKEP into a hydrolysate of DH > 70% within 6 h of hydrolysis.
the PKEP was effectively hydrolyzed by Alcalase®2.4L to produce PKEPH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzymatic hydrolytic process of the PKEP is an alternative to the production of high quality protein hydrolysates with high DH% that could be used as a source of protein for human consumption.
the PKEP is a good substrate to produce protein hydrolysate using Alcalase®.
PKEP can be effectively extracted and hydrolyzed to produce a high DH hydrolysate (81.35%).
